newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council says police important for peacekeeping.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council says police important for peacekeeping.

text.p: The Security Council encouraged states on Monday to make appropriately trained police available at short notice for U.N. peacekeeping operations.

A statement read at a brief public meeting said civilian police performed indispensable functions in monitoring and training national police forces and could play a major role, through assistance to local police, in restoring civil order and fostering civil reconciliation.
The statement was the result of an initiative by Sweden, which currently has police serving with the United Nations in Angola, Croatia's Eastern Slavonia region and Bosnia.
Sweden holds the presidency of the council this month and the statement was read by Swedish Foreign Minister Lena Hjelm-Wallen, who chaired the meeting.
"The Security Council underlines the importance of the recruitment of qualified civilian police from the widest possible geographic range to serve in United Nations operations," the statement said.
"It also expresses the importance of the recruitment of female police officers to United Nations operations."
Secretary-General Kofi Annan was asked to help U.N. members create a standardised approach to training and recruiting civilian police.
